articles.title: Guna School Fancy Dress Political Stunt: MP Child Rights Commission probes anti-democratic act; ABVP slams school
articles.description: BHOPAL: The Madhya Pradesh Child Rights Protection Commission has taken serious note of a fancy dress performance by a Class 1 girl at Christ Senior Secondary School in Guna district. Meanwhile, the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) registered its protest and submitted a memorandum to the school principal, demanding an explanation. The incident is said to have taken place on 13 October. It is alleged that the school’s fancy dress performance targeted democracy and constitutional institutions, especially the government, and sought to convey that governments at the Centre and in the state have taken away ordinary citizens’ right to speak, and that a dictatorship prevails in the country. Dr Nivedita Sharma, chairperson of the Madhya Pradesh Child Rights Protection Commission, said plainly that no feeling against democracy, constitutional institutions or the government can be instilled in the tender minds of children. She warned that if any attempt is made, under any pretext, to teach hatred in schools, the centres of education, action will be taken in accordance with the rules. At a fancy dress competition held at one Christ school in Guna, Madhya Pradesh, a primary class student appeared with two banners attached to her dress One banner said – ‘democracy has been expelled from school because it asked questions’ Another banner said –‘School of the… pic.twitter.com/1Gvs3elq0x — Swati Goel Sharma (@swati_gs) October 15, 2026 Dr Sharma said: “The purpose of education is for children to receive a good education, become successful citizens of the country, bring glory to the state and the nation across the world, and succeed in their own lives in every field. But if small children are used in schools to carry political messages, that is a direct violation of child rights.” The Commission has said it will issue directions to the officials concerned to investigate, and has sought a detailed report from the school management, the district education department and other parties concerned. Read More: ‘Stop Anarchy, Embrace Democracy’: ABVP leads campus rallies in Himachal & Varanasi against anarchist tactics Class 1 Girl Displays Political Messages on Stage On Tuesday, a fancy dress competition was held at Christ Senior Secondary School in Guna for pupils from Class 1 to Class 5. During it, a Class 1 girl came on stage in her school uniform with a band tied across her mouth. She held a large placard in her hand, and another hung from her back. The placard in her hand read: “Sarkar ki Pathshala (The Government’s School)… Attendance Sheet Unemployment: Present, Sir Hatred: Present, Sir Corruption: Present, Sir Terrorism: Present, Sir Inflation: Present, Sir Poverty: Present, Sir Democracy: Absent, Sir Vote theft: Present, Sir Paper leak: Present, Sir Scams: Present, Sir” The placard hanging from her back carried an even sharper message: “Democracy was expelled from the school because it asked questions…” Photographs and video of the performance went viral on social media. A debate broke out in the city’s political and social circles over whether it is appropriate for such a young girl to be used to deliver such pointed political messages at a private school’s cultural event. ABVP Submits Memorandum As soon as it learnt of the incident, the Guna unit of the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) swung into action. Its workers submitted a memorandum to the school principal and lodged a strong objection. The ABVP said that the purpose of academic and cultural programmes should be to promote students’ talent, creativity and personality development. Displaying political messages through innocent children on such platforms, it said, runs contrary to academic dignity. ‘Democracy Expelled’: Class 1 Student Paraded With Anti-Govt Political Messages At Christ Senior Secondary School In MP, Management Blames Parents https://t.co/ysuZgR2Nid via @The Commune — Samskarebyaha "Modi Ka Parivar" (@samskarebyaha) October 16, 2026 The ABVP’s clear position is that such a stage performance could not have taken place without the school’s permission, and that, even if it was happening, the school administration should have tried to stop it immediately. If no such attempt was made, it said, it will be assumed that the school administration gave this negative effort its tacit support. The Parishad demanded an impartial inquiry into the role of the event in-charge and the teachers concerned. It also asked that the matter be reported to the District Education Officer and the Child Rights Protection Commission, and that the school management clarify its official stance. The ABVP warned that, if satisfactory action is not taken, it will file a statutory complaint before the child rights and education authorities. As the controversy grew, the school’s principal, Father Babu Tharayil CMI, issued an official clarification. The management said the girl’s costume did not conform to the guidelines laid down for the competition. The school claims the decision was entirely the parents’ and that they had dressed the child at home and sent her. The management said it had issued a show-cause notice to the teacher in charge of the programme, and that monitoring would be increased to prevent such incidents from recurring. Congress Leaders Share Pictures; Political Colour Deepens According to another piece of information related to the episode, the girl who took part in the fancy dress competition is reportedly the granddaughter of a senior Congress leader of the city, though there is no independent confirmation of this. Several senior Congress leaders, including the Congress district president and Raghogarh MLA Jaivardhan Singh, shared pictures of the girl’s costume on social media. It has emerged that these posts were used to target the BJP government. Some citizens of the city also questioned whether it was wrong for a private school to make such an attempt. articles.title: Govt halts sugar-based ethanol procurement as weak monsoon hurts output
articles.description: The Centre has directed state-owned fuel retailers to stop procuring ethanol made from sugar and key sugarcane-based feedstocks in a move aimed at keeping a lid on sugar prices. The direction will take effect from the new supply year starting November 1 after dry weather hits sugarcane production, according to the tender document.PSU refiners -- Indian Oil Corp Ltd (IOCL), Bharat Petroleum Corp Ltd (BPCL), Hindustan Petroleum Corp Ltd (HPCL), Numaligarh Refinery Ltd and Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd -- have issued a joint tender seeking nearly 11 billion litres of ethanol for the new supply year, citing the new government directions."No offers have been sought for ethanol produced from sugarcane juice, sugar, sugar syrup and B-Heavy molasses in this quantity bid tender," according to the document. India -- the world's second-biggest sugar producer -- faces a smaller crop than a year earlier after El Nino contributed to the weakest monsoon in more than a decade. The nation has increasingly used sugarcane and grains to produce ethanol as part of efforts to curb dependence on imported oil. Moreover, the government had brought forward its target of blending 20 per cent ethanol into gasoline by five years and achieved the goal in 2025. Suppliers participating in the latest tender can offer ethanol produced from C-heavy molasses, damaged food grains, surplus rice procured from Food Corp of India, corn and other feedstocks permitted under the National Policy on Biofuels. Apart from that, the government has permitted sugar mills to sell sugar produced in October 2026 during October and November 2026 over and above the regular monthly release quotas. As per the government order, if a sugar mill produces 1,000 MT of sugar during October, it may sell the quantity during October and November, in addition to quantities allocated under regular monthly release quotas.
